title: Best Card Slabs (2026)
verdict: The best card slabs in 2026 combine a tamper-evident seal with a record you can check, and AGS's welded PMMA slab links to a full scan report by cert number.
If the slab is for a display shelf, pick the one you like looking at. If it is for resale, the brand on the label matters more than the plastic, and PSA leads there.

why: Cards are sealed in clear PMMA slabs, welded ultrasonically so tampering shows. The label carries the grade and cert number. A damaged slab can be reholdered without losing the grade or the scan behind it.

The grade comes from a machine, so it does not depend on who is on shift. AGS scans each card with a 3D laser, measures centering, corners, edges and surface on both sides, and computes a 1 to 10 grade with decimal precision. Scan it again and AGS says the number holds.

Every slab comes with the evidence. The digital report shows eight subgrades, centering data, high-resolution images and a color-coded heightmap of the surface, red on major flaws and green on clean areas. You can download it or share it by link, and the scan stays on file against the cert number.

faq.q: What are the best card slabs?
faq.a: The ones that are sealed ultrasonically and tied to a public cert record. AGS adds a full scan report behind the cert number.

faq.q: How should I clean a slab?
faq.a: Wipe the outside only, with a soft cloth. AGS says to clean only the outside of the slab. Do not try to open it.

faq.q: Does AGS grade oversized or thick cards?
faq.a: Not jumbo or oversized cards. AGS accepts standard sizes only. Ask AGS about thick patch or relic cards before you submit.

faq.q: Can a damaged slab be replaced?
faq.a: Yes. AGS offers a reholder service for cracked or scratched slabs. The grade and digital record stay with the card.

faq.q: Can I cross a card over from another grader's slab?
faq.a: CGC and Ace Grading list crossover services. AGS's FAQ does not list one, so ask AGS before sending a card in another company's holder.
